solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Bright wife, Russian woman from the east

indicators.note: in an across clue, reading from the east means going right to left, so the pieces are turned round

parts.note: Olga is a typical Russian woman's name

explanation.surface: A man describes his radiant wife, a Russian woman who came from the east.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from the east' turns W + OLGA round to read right to left.
explanation.definitionFit: Something glowing with light or warmth is shining, a plain synonym of bright.

clue.text: Complaint to hotel — feast is awful

indicators.note: something awful is a mess, so the letters of these words are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A guest complains to the hotel that the banquet was terrible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awful' rearranges the twelve letters of TO HOTEL FEAST; 'is' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A complaint in the medical sense is an ailment, and this fungal infection of the toes is a common one.

clue.text: Injured leg broken by car without front bumper

indicators.note: the jumbled leg is split open with the other piece set inside it
an injured leg is damaged and out of shape, so its letters are rearranged
the car loses its front letter

explanation.surface: A driver's leg was hurt in a collision with a car that had lost its front bumper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bumper' looks like part of the car, but it is the adjective meaning big, as in a bumper crop.
explanation.definitionFit: A bumper crop or harvest is an exceptionally big one, so bumper is a synonym of the adjective.

clue.text: Sally is on drugs, after whiskey

indicators.note: the whiskey piece comes first, with the rest following after it
in a down clue one piece sits on top of another, so the is piece comes above the drugs

parts.note: Whiskey is W in the NATO phonetic alphabet
E is ecstasy and crack is cocaine in rock form: two drugs

explanation.surface: A woman named Sally is on drugs after drinking whiskey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sally' looks like a woman's name, but it is a witty remark. 'drugs' supplies two pieces, E and CRACK.
explanation.definitionFit: A sally is a quick witty retort, the same thing as a smart-alec joke.

clue.text: What's left is due to get pickled in alcohol

indicators.note: the jumbled letters are placed inside the alcohol

parts.note: rum is an alcoholic spirit

indicators.note: pickled is slang for drunk, so the letters are muddled up

explanation.surface: Whatever remains is due to get preserved in spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pickled' is British slang for drunk, which suits the alcohol in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A residuum is a remainder or residue, the part left over after a process.

clue.text: Concerned with tax break

parts.note: re means about or concerning, as in business letters
a cess is an old word for a tax or levy

explanation.surface: Someone worried about a tax break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Concerned with tax' reads as one phrase, but 'break' is the definition on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: A recess is a pause or interval, as when a court or parliament takes a break.

clue.text: Old, dishy models in second-rate fashion

indicators.note: to model is to shape or form, so the letters are shaped into a new order

explanation.surface: Elderly but attractive fashion models wearing cheap clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'models' looks like a noun for catwalk people, but it is a verb rearranging OLD DISHY.
explanation.definitionFit: Shoddy means poorly made or inferior, so acting this way is behaving in a second-rate manner.

clue.text: Men charge, capturing duke

indicators.note: the charge piece takes the duke prisoner, holding it inside

parts.note: dues are charges or fees, such as membership dues

explanation.surface: Soldiers charge forward and take a duke prisoner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charge' looks like a military verb but gives DUES.
explanation.definitionFit: Dudes is informal American slang for guys or fellows.

clue.text: Remove cover from horse — dislodge man astride it

indicators.note: the pieces sit on either side of the horse, as a rider does when astride it

parts.note: to unseat is to throw off or dislodge, as a rider
horse is slang for heroin, abbreviated H
he is a pronoun for a man

explanation.surface: A rider is thrown from his horse as it bucks him off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'horse' is not an animal but drug slang for heroin, H, and 'it' points back to that horse.
explanation.definitionFit: To unsheathe a sword is to draw it out of its scabbard, taking away its protective cover.

clue.text: Player of instruments, one group of notes first

parts.note: harps are stringed musical instruments
I is the Roman numeral for one
a chord is several notes sounded together
first can be written 1st, which reads as IST with the figure taken as a letter I

explanation.surface: A musician leading a group of players, one who plays the first notes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Player of instruments' reads as the definition, but only 'Player' is; 'first' written as 1ST supplies IST.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who plays the harpsichord, a keyboard instrument, is a kind of player.

clue.text: Not accommodating endlessly travelling fellow

indicators.note: without an end, the phrase loses its final letter

parts.note: in transit means on the way or travelling
gent is short for gentleman, a fellow

explanation.surface: A fellow who is always on the move is not accommodating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts the last T from IN TRANSIT, leaving INTRANSI.
explanation.definitionFit: Intransigent means refusing to compromise or budge, the opposite of accommodating.

clue.text: Did train cut around borders of Ecuador?

indicators.note: the cut piece wraps around the letters taken from Ecuador

parts.note: to excise is to cut out

indicators.note: the borders of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A question about whether a train service was cut along Ecuador's borders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'train' looks like a railway noun but is a verb: exercised means trained or worked out. 'borders of Ecuador' gives E and R.
explanation.definitionFit: To exercise is to drill or work out, so the past tense is a synonym of did train.

clue.text: Serious Irish novelist hasn't finished

indicators.note: the novelist is left without a finish, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: Laurence Sterne, author of Tristram Shandy, was born in Ireland

explanation.surface: A grave Irish author who has not yet completed his novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hasn't finished' fits Sterne, whose Tristram Shandy famously rambles on unfinished.
explanation.definitionFit: Stern means grave and severe in manner, a synonym of serious.

clue.text: Make popular organ stop at first

indicators.note: the stop piece is placed at the start, before the organ

parts.note: to end is to stop
the ear is the organ of hearing

explanation.surface: An organist pulls out a stop first to win over the audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organ stop' reads as a single musical term on the surface, but the two words are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To endear someone is to cause them to be liked, so it means make popular.

clue.text: New media star put on stage, say

indicators.note: something new is made afresh, so the letters are formed into a new order

explanation.surface: A fresh celebrity from the media is cast in a theatre production.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' rearranges MEDIA STAR.
explanation.definitionFit: To dramatise a story is to adapt it as a play; staging it is one example, hence 'say'.

clue.text: Bachelor having lost weight is a villain

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for bachelor, as in BA
after losing weight one is lighter

explanation.surface: A single man who has slimmed down turns out to be a bad lot.
explanation.definitionFit: A blighter is an old British slang term for a scoundrel or rotter.

clue.text: Sort of coffee and fruitcake for a snack

parts.note: ground coffee is one sort, as against instant or beans
fruitcake is slang for a crazy person, a nut

explanation.surface: Coffee and fruitcake served as a little snack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fruitcake' looks like food but means a madman, NUT.
explanation.definitionFit: Peanuts are also known by this name, and they are eaten as a snack.

clue.text: Mean to develop The Times's charms

indicators.note: to develop is to change or grow, so the letters of mean change into a new order

parts.note: a newspaper speaking of itself says ours, as The Times is the setter's paper

explanation.surface: The newspaper means to develop its own appeal to readers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to develop' rearranges MEAN into ENAM; the paper's own possession is OURS.
explanation.definitionFit: To enamour someone is to fill them with love, much as to charm or captivate them.

clue.text: Edging from the best pastry chef?

parts.note: a flan is a pastry case with a filling
a king of something is the best at it, as in a pastry chef hailed as king

explanation.surface: A question about where a fine pastry comes from, the work of a top chef.
explanation.walkthrough: The champion pastry chef might be dubbed the flan king; 'chef?' completes that whimsical picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Flanking means lying along the side of something, as a border edging it does.

clue.text: Single month, November or August?

parts.note: sole means only or single
November is N in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Picking one month for an event: November or August?
explanation.walkthrough: 'August' seems to be a month like November, but it is the adjective meaning dignified.
explanation.definitionFit: August as an adjective means venerable and dignified, the same tone as grave and serious.

clue.text: Maybe a little salt, holding back in fast food

indicators.note: the grain contains the extra letter within it

parts.note: a grain is a tiny amount, such as a grain of salt; maybe marks it as one example

indicators.note: the back of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A snack bar meal, perhaps lightly salted, with the salt held back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fast food' reads as one phrase, but 'fast' only gives its last letter T, and 'food' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A gratin is a dish topped with browned breadcrumbs or cheese, so it is a kind of food.

clue.text: Round motorway, I see US city

parts.note: O is round in shape
M is a British motorway, as in the M1
aha is what you say when you see or understand

explanation.surface: Driving the ring road around a motorway, someone spots an American city.
explanation.definitionFit: Omaha is the largest city in Nebraska, a place in the United States.

clue.text: Is one seen in Hampden Park tie?

parts.note: a means one
Hampden Park in Glasgow is Scotland's national football stadium, full of Scots

explanation.surface: Asking whether a certain necktie is worn at a Scottish football ground.
explanation.walkthrough: Hampden Park is Scotland's national football stadium in Glasgow, so a typical spectator there is a Scot.
explanation.definitionFit: An ascot is a broad neckcloth or cravat, a type of necktie.

clue.text: Soldier not drinking with one Italian poet

parts.note: a marine is a soldier who serves at sea
TT means teetotal
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A sober soldier keeps company with an Italian poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Filippo Tommaso Marinetti was the Italian writer who founded Futurism.

clue.text: Aussie can start to travel, visiting US city

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

parts.note: someone visiting a place is in it
NY is New York

explanation.surface: An Australian who can begin to travel goes to see an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Aussie can' looks like an Australian who is able, but it is a beer can.
explanation.definitionFit: In Australian slang a tinny is a can of beer.

clue.text: Frown on policeman's face

parts.note: a DI is a detective inspector, so a policeman's gives DI'S
a countenance is a face

explanation.surface: A disapproving frown on a police officer's face.
explanation.definitionFit: To discountenance something is to disapprove of it, to look on it with disfavour.

clue.text: Scrap metal plating thus put on aircraft

indicators.note: the plated piece is added on after the aircraft

parts.note: a jet is a jet-propelled aircraft

indicators.note: the metal coats the other piece on either side, as plating covers an object

parts.note: tin is a metal
so means thus, in this way

explanation.surface: Scrap metal plating is fitted onto an aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scrap metal' reads as a phrase, but 'Scrap' alone is the verb defining the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To jettison is to throw away or discard, which is what you do when you scrap something.

clue.text: Taste skin of succulent date

parts.note: to try food is to taste it

indicators.note: the skin of a word is its outer letters

explanation.surface: Sampling the soft skin of a juicy date fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'date' looks like the fruit, but it is a romantic meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: A tryst is a secret romantic meeting between lovers, a kind of date.
